_meta.note: TDS client and server message definitions. Messages are framed in TDS packets (8-byte header + payload).

packet_header.description: All TDS messages are wrapped in packets with an 8-byte header

structure.desc: Total packet length including header (512-32767 bytes per negotiated size)
Server Process ID; server sets this; client sends 0x0000
Sequence counter 1-255, wraps to 1 (not 0). Resets to 0 on new connection.

packet_types.0x12: PRELOGIN (client→server; also used for TLS handshake encapsulation in TDS 7.x)

all_headers.description: ALL_HEADERS structure prepended to SQLBatch, RPC, and TransactionManagerRequest messages

structure.desc: Total byte count of ALL_HEADERS structure including TotalLength field itself

fields.desc: Length of this header including HeaderLength field
Current transaction descriptor from ENVCHANGE type 8
Number of open requests on current connection; typically 1

messages.name: PRELOGIN
messages.description: Initial handshake. Client sends version, encryption support, MARS support, and optional trace/nonce info. Server responds with its own PRELOGIN. In TDS 7.x, TLS handshake follows using PRELOGIN packet type.

structure.format: Option token table followed by option data
structure.option_table: PL_OPTION_TOKEN(1) + Offset(2, big-endian) + Length(2, big-endian) repeated for each option, terminated by TERMINATOR(0xFF)

option_tokens.name: VERSION
option_tokens.format: MajorVer(1) + MinorVer(1) + SubBuild(2, little-endian) + Build(2, little-endian)

values.0x80: ENCRYPT_CLIENT_CERT (bit; sent as 0x80 with OFF, 0x81 with ON, 0x83 with REQ)

option_tokens.name: TRACEID
option_tokens.format: ConnectionID(16 bytes GUID) + ActivityID(16 bytes GUID) + ActivitySeq(4 bytes ULONG)

encryption_negotiation_matrix.description: Final encryption determined by combining client and server ENCRYPTION values
rules: Client ENCRYPT_ON + Server ENCRYPT_ON → Encrypt all
Client ENCRYPT_ON + Server ENCRYPT_NOT_SUP → Connection failed
Client ENCRYPT_NOT_SUP + Server ENCRYPT_ON → Encrypt login only (TDS 7.x) or Connection failed (TDS 8.0)
Client ENCRYPT_OFF + Server ENCRYPT_OFF → No encryption
Client ENCRYPT_REQ + any Server not ENCRYPT_REQ → Connection failed
TDS 8.0: TLS established before PRELOGIN, so encryption always active

messages.name: LOGIN7
messages.description: Client login request. Complex fixed-header + variable-length data section + optional FeatureExt.

fixed_header_fields.desc: fByteOrder(1=big-endian), fChar(1=EBCDIC), fFloat(2-bit: 0=IEEE754 LE, 1=IEEE754 BE, 2=VAX), fDumpLoad, fUseDB, fDatabase, fSetLang
fLanguage, fODBC, fTransBoundary, fCacheConnect, fUserType(3-bit: 0=normal, 1=server, 2=remuser, 3=sqlrepl), fIntSecurity(1=integrated security/SSPI)
fChangePassword, fSendYukonBinaryXML, fUserInstance, fUnknownCollationHandling, fExtension(1=FeatureExt present)

ibHostName/cchHostName, ibUserName/cchUserName, ibPassword/cchPassword, ibAppName/cchAppName, ibServerName/cchServerName, ibExtension/cbExtension, ibCltIntName/cchCltIntName, ibLanguage/cchLanguage, ibDatabase/cchDatabase, ibClientID(6 bytes), ibSSPI/cbSSPI, ibAtchDBFile/cchAtchDBFile, ibChangePassword/cchChangePassword
If cbSSPI > 0xFFFF use this field for actual SSPI length

messages.variable_data: Hostname + Username + Password + AppName + ServerName + Extension(FeatureExt if fExtension=1) + InterfaceName + Language + Database + ClientID(6) + SSPI + AttachDBFile + NewPassword
messages.password_encoding: Swap high and low nibbles of each byte, then XOR with 0xA5. Encoded in UTF-16LE.

feature_ext.description: Optional feature negotiation appended to LOGIN7 data when OptionFlags3.fExtension=1
feature_ext.format: 1*FeatureExtOpt terminated by TERMINATOR(0xFF). Each FeatureExtOpt: FeatureId(1) + FeatureDataLen(4) + FeatureData.

feature_ids.name: FEDAUTH
feature_ids.data_format: bFedAuthLibrary(1) + bFedAuthEcho(1 bit) + [token data based on bFedAuthLibrary]

messages.name: SQLBatch
messages.description: Sends one or more SQL statements as Unicode text.
notes: EnclavePackage only for Always Encrypted with enclave computations (TDS 7.4)

messages.name: RPC
messages.description: Remote Procedure Call. Calls stored procedures by name (US_VARCHAR) or well-known ProcID. Client sends typed parameters; server returns RETURNSTATUS + RETURNVALUE* for output params.

proc_id_switch.note: CRITICAL: US_VARCHAR and B_VARCHAR use CHARACTER count in the length prefix, NOT byte count. Server reads length_field * 2 bytes of UTF-16LE data. Writing byte count (chars * 2) instead of char count doubles the server's read length → 'TDS stream incorrect'.
proc_id_switch.user_proc_by_name: US_VARCHAR: USHORT(char_count) + UTF-16LE chars. No 0xFFFF prefix for named procs.

string_length_encoding.US_VARCHAR: USHORT = character count (NOT byte count). Then character_count * 2 bytes of UTF-16LE follow. Used for: procedure names, some other string fields. USHORT max = 65535 chars.
string_length_encoding.B_VARCHAR: BYTE = character count (NOT byte count). Then character_count * 2 bytes of UTF-16LE follow. Used for: parameter names, column names, short strings. BYTE max = 255 chars.
string_length_encoding.US_VARBYTE: USHORT = byte count. Then byte_count bytes follow. Used for binary data, SSPI tokens.
string_length_encoding.B_VARBYTE: BYTE = byte count. Then byte_count bytes follow.
string_length_encoding.swift_read_example: readUSVarchar(): readUShort() → N chars, then readUTF16String(length: N*2). readBVarchar(): readByte() → N chars, then readUTF16String(length: N*2).
string_length_encoding.swift_write_example: For US_VARCHAR proc name: buffer.writeInteger(UInt16(procChars.count), endianness: .little) — NOT procChars.count*2 (byte count).

messages.option_flags: 2 bytes: Bit 0x0001=WITH RECOMPILE, Bit 0x0002=NoMetaData (server sends COLMETADATA 0xFFFF)

fields.desc: Parameter name including @; max 128 chars. Length=0 for unnamed params. Server returns this name (with @) in RETURNVALUE tokens.
0x00=input, 0x01=ByRef (output parameter). Server sends RETURNVALUE for each output parameter.
Type hint for the parameter. Server uses declared parameter type for conversion.

type_encoding_by_kind.INTN: 0x26 + MaxLen(1: 1/2/4/8) + ByteLen(1: 0=null, else=MaxLen) + data. MaxLen=0 is INVALID — always use 1/2/4/8.
type_encoding_by_kind.NVARCHAR: 0xE7 + MaxLen(2, byte count, e.g. 8000 for NVARCHAR(4000)) + Collation(5) + ActualLen(2, byte count, 0xFFFF=null) + UTF-16LE data.
type_encoding_by_kind.VARCHAR: 0xA7 + MaxLen(2, byte count, e.g. 8000) + Collation(5) + ActualLen(2, 0xFFFF=null) + bytes.
type_encoding_by_kind.null_placeholder_for_out: When param.data is nil for an OUTPUT param, send NVARCHAR(8000) NULL: 0xE7 + 0x40 0x1F + 5-zero-collation + 0xFF 0xFF. Server uses the declared parameter type regardless of client type hint.
type_encoding_by_kind.TDSData_string_note: TDSData(string:) stores UTF-16LE bytes with .varchar metadata (historical). In RPC encoding, re-emit as NVARCHAR to avoid server interpreting UTF-16LE bytes as single-byte varchar characters.

messages.server_response_token_order: RETURNSTATUS(0x79, Int32) → RETURNVALUE*(0xAC, one per output param) → [COLMETADATA + ROW*] → DONEINPROC* → DONEPROC
known_bugs_fixed_sqlserver_nio: FIXED 2026-03-04: US_VARCHAR proc name wrote byte count (chars*2) instead of char count → 'TDS stream incorrect'
FIXED 2026-03-04: NULL param encoding sent INTN MaxLen=0 (invalid) → use NVARCHAR(8000) NULL for unknown-type out params
FIXED 2026-03-04: nvarchar maxLen used actual value byte count (0 for empty string) → use 8000 as default maxLen
FIXED 2026-03-04: TokenHandler.onReturnValue called callback twice (once directly, once via tokenHandler) → doubled return values
FIXED 2026-03-04: call() returnValues never populated (missing onReturnValue callback in RpcRequest)

messages.name: BulkLoad
messages.description: Bulk insert data. Initiated by INSERT BULK T-SQL statement. Binary data stream, not token-based.
messages.structure: Binary data matching the format described by the INSERT BULK statement metadata

messages.name: Attention
messages.description: Requests server cancel the current outstanding request. No payload — header only. Server acknowledges with DONE token (DONE_ATTN bit set).

messages.name: FederatedAuthToken
messages.description: Sends federated authentication token to server after receiving FEDAUTHINFO.
messages.structure: TokenLength(4) + Token bytes + [Nonce signature if applicable]

messages.name: SSPI
messages.description: SPNEGO/SSPI security token. Initial token sent in LOGIN7 body; subsequent exchanges use SSPI message type. Server responds with SSPI token or final LOGINACK.

messages.name: TransactionManagerRequest
messages.description: Transaction control (begin, commit, rollback, savepoint, DTC).

request_types.name: TM_GET_DTC_ADDRESS
request_types.response: Single-column binary result set with DTC network address

request_types.name: TM_PROPAGATE_XACT
request_types.response: Local transaction descriptor in varbinary result set

request_types.name: TM_PROMOTE_XACT
request_types.note: TDS 7.2+; promotes local transaction to distributed; only for transactions started by TM_BEGIN_XACT or piggybacked

request_types.name: TM_COMMIT_XACT
request_types.payload: XACT_NAME(B_VARBYTE) + XACT_FLAGS(BYTE: fBeginXact+7reserved) + [ISOLATION_LEVEL if fBeginXact=1] + [BEGIN_XACT_NAME if fBeginXact=1]

request_types.name: TM_ROLLBACK_XACT
request_types.note: TDS 7.2+; if XACT_NAME=savepoint name, rolls back to savepoint only

notes: For MARS-capable clients, explicit transactions should use TransactionManagerRequest messages; issuing raw SQL BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK without updating the client transaction descriptor breaks subsequent SQLBatch/RPC framing.
While an explicit transaction is active, every SQLBatch, RPC, and TransactionManagerRequest MUST carry the current transaction descriptor in ALL_HEADERS.TransactionDescriptor.
The transaction descriptor value is learned from ENVCHANGE type 8 and cleared when ENVCHANGE type 9, 10, or 17 is received.

messages.name: TabularResult (Login Response)
messages.description: Server response to LOGIN7. Contains token stream: [ENVCHANGE...] LOGINACK [FEATUREEXTACK] DONE

messages.name: TabularResult (Query Response)
messages.description: Server response to SQLBatch or RPC. Token stream varies by query type.
notes: Under MARS, query requests inside an explicit transaction must reuse the current transaction descriptor in ALL_HEADERS; a zero descriptor is only valid when no explicit transaction is active.
Clients should treat ENVCHANGE types 8, 9, 10, and 17 as connection-level transaction state updates, not just informational tokens.

known_issues_sqlserver_nio.title: TDS Version: Must negotiate 7.3+ for native date/time types
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.symptom: DATE, TIME, DATETIME2, DATETIMEOFFSET columns returned as nvarchar strings instead of native types
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.root_cause: Login7Message.swift was sending TDS 7.2 (0x72090002). SQL Server downconverts newer types to nvarchar for TDS 7.2 clients.
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.fix: Login7Message.swift: changed TDS version bytes to 7.4 (0x04000074 → bytes [0x04, 0x00, 0x00, 0x74]). TDS 7.3+ is the minimum for native DATE/TIME/DATETIME2/DATETIMEOFFSET.

known_issues_sqlserver_nio.title: BYTELEN_TYPE (date/time) row values need 1-byte length prefix read
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.symptom: DATE, TIME, DATETIME2, DATETIMEOFFSET columns decode incorrectly; null handling broken
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.root_cause: TDSTokenParser.swift parseColumnValue() was reading fixed-length bytes directly. With TDS 7.3+, these types are BYTELEN_TYPE: each row value has a 1-byte length prefix (0x00=null, N=N data bytes).
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.fix: parseColumnValue() case .date, .time, .datetime2, .datetimeOffset: use readByteLengthPayload(nullMarker: 0x00) to read the 1-byte length prefix first.
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.tds_ref: §2.2.5.5.1.5 BYTELEN_TYPE, §2.2.5.4 type date 0x28, time 0x29, datetime2 0x2A, datetimeoffset 0x2B

known_issues_sqlserver_nio.title: COLMETADATA scale byte double-read for time/datetime2/datetimeoffset
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.symptom: SELECT returning time/datetime2/datetimeoffset columns parses 0 tokens; query appears to hang or stall
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.root_cause: TDSTokenParser+ColMetadata.swift length switch fell through to 'default' case (reads 1 byte as length) for time/datetime2/datetimeoffset. Then isScaleType()=true read ANOTHER byte as scale. Two bytes consumed where one expected → buffer misaligned → needMoreData loop.
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.fix: Add explicit cases in the ColMetadata length switch: case .time, .datetime2, .datetimeOffset: length = 0 (no length byte; scale byte handled separately by isScaleType path). Case .date: length = 3 (DATE has no scale).
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.tds_ref: §2.2.5.5.1.3 FIXEDLENTYPE, TYPE_INFO for time/datetime2/datetimeoffset have only a Scale byte, no MaxLen.

known_issues_sqlserver_nio.title: listColumns concurrent calls trigger N full-schema queries
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.symptom: listColumns() for N tables in the same schema concurrently causes timeout (10s per operation) for large schemas (AdventureWorks Production/Sales with 25+ tables)
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.root_cause: schema_catalog mode called listColumnsForSchema() which runs loadColumnsFromCatalogForDatabase() — a full-schema JOIN query. N concurrent calls = N full-schema queries on the DB simultaneously. Cache only helped after first query completed, not for concurrent starters.
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.fix: Changed listColumns() schema_catalog path to call loadColumnsFromCatalog(isView:false, includeDefaultMetadata:true) — a fast per-table query. This also provides defaultDefinition. isView=false is safe for both tables and views (view columns have no default/computed constraints so LEFT JOINs return NULL naturally). Also removed unnecessary isViewObject() round-trip query when willUseSchemaBulk=true.
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.performance: SQLServerMetadataAnalysisTests: 90/90 tables in 19s (was 64s failing at 60s budget)

known_issues_sqlserver_nio.title: loadColumnsFromCatalogForDatabase missing defaultDefinition (default constraint text)
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.symptom: Column metadata for tables returns hasDefaultValue=true but defaultDefinition=nil even when column has a DEFAULT constraint
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.root_cause: loadColumnsFromCatalogForDatabase (bulk schema query) only checked c.default_object_id != 0 for hasDefaultValue but didn't join sys.default_constraints to get the definition text.
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.fix: Added LEFT JOIN sys.default_constraints AS dc ON c.default_object_id = dc.object_id AND o.type = 'U' and CAST(dc.definition AS NVARCHAR(4000)) AS default_definition to the SELECT.
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.note: View columns naturally return NULL for default_definition (views have no default constraints) so the same query works for both tables and views.

known_issues_sqlserver_nio.title: TDSPacket decoder reads header from absolute offset 0 instead of readerIndex — multi-packet stall
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.symptom: Queries returning large result sets (many TDS packets) stall indefinitely or until commandTimeout fires. Small result sets (1 packet) work fine.
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.root_cause: TDSPacketDecoder.decode() runs a while loop to consume multiple TDS packets per TCP segment. TDSPacket.init?(from:) read the packet header using buffer.getInteger(at: 0) and buffer.getInteger(at: 2) — absolute indices from the buffer's origin. After the first packet was consumed via buffer.readSlice(), readerIndex advanced to N bytes. The second iteration still read from at:0 (first packet's stale type/length bytes). When the last short packet arrived, the stale 'length' exceeded readableBytes → returned nil → decode loop exited with .needMoreData → permanent stall.
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.fix: TDSPacket.swift init?(from buffer: inout ByteBuffer): save let ri = buffer.readerIndex before reading header fields. Use buffer.getInteger(at: ri) for typeByte and buffer.getInteger(at: ri + 2) for length.

known_issues_sqlserver_nio.title: Historical stall/hang fixes — see Docs/test-stall-fix.txt
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.description: Complete history of TDS protocol stall fixes is documented in the sqlserver-nio repo at Docs/test-stall-fix.txt. Key fixes include: packet decoder header at readerIndex (not offset 0), token parser not consuming unknown bytes, request buffer hygiene on completion, ALL_HEADERS transaction descriptor on every batch, ENVCHANGE updating connection state, PLP/NVARCHAR(MAX) cast to NVARCHAR(4000) in metadata queries.

known_issues_sqlserver_nio.title: readUTF16String(length:) expects UTF-16 code units, not raw byte count
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.symptom: nvarchar/nchar values and other UTF-16 payloads decode as nil or appear truncated/garbled.
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.root_cause: The ByteBuffer helper multiplies the supplied length by 2 before reading. Callers that passed readableBytes instead of readableBytes / 2 tried to consume twice the payload.
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.fix: When decoding an in-memory UTF-16 payload, first validate readableBytes is even and then call readUTF16String(length: readableBytes / 2).

known_issues_sqlserver_nio.title: Connection-backed metadata and agent facades must not escape withConnection closures
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.symptom: Metadata or Agent calls intermittently fail with connection closed after a facade was constructed inside client.withConnection { ... } and then reused later.
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.root_cause: SQLServerMetadataOperations created from a SQLServerConnection is tied to that checkout. After the closure returns, the pooled connection can be released or invalidated while the facade is still retained.
known_issues_sqlserver_nio.fix: Use client-scoped entry points such as SQLServerClient.fetchAgentStatus() or SQLServerAgentOperations(client: client) when the operation should span pooled connection checkouts.
